full_judgment:
3. The plaintiff’s case, in brief, is that the suit land originally belonged to one Paimullah Kabiraj and he died leaving behind four sons and two daughters. The plaintiffs predecessor-in-interest Kali Kumar Pal; purchased the suit land from the said heirs of Paimullah Kabiraj by registered deed No. 1406 dated 24.3.42 It is also the case of the plaintiff that during the SA Operation the suit land was recorded in the name of the plaintiff and some of the defendants. Thereafter the plaintiff filed a case before the revenue authority under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. After hearing, plaintiff's case was allowed and the defendants names were struck out and the name of the sole plaintiff was substituted in the record of right by order dated 24.6.75 passed by the Additional Circle Officer, Revenue, Parbatipur. The plaintiff further asserted that he has althrough been in possession of the suit land since purchased in the year 1951 and before that their predecessor-in-interest had been in possession of the land. 

 10. He further argues that the volume book from registrar office was called for by the trial Court at the instance of the plaintiff but from PW 5 a staff of the sub-Registrar Office who brought the volume book before the Court in cross-examination stated that it appears from the volume book that one of the 7 executants did not give his thumb impression on the deed. 

 11. Mr. Abdul Hameed Chowdhury also contends that Court rightly observed that the husband's names of 3 of the executants as appearing on the deed (Certified Copy) and as stated in the plaint are not exactly same. 

 12. In reply to the above submission Mr. Munsur Habib, the learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite parties submits that the said deed dated 24.3.42 is a deed of over 30 years old. And the plaintiff has stated in his evidence that he never had the possession of the said deed and so he could not produce it before the Court and for that through Court he called for the volume book from the sub-registrar's Office and filed a certified copy of the said deed which was marked as Ext. 5(d). He argues that the execution of the deed being over 30 years old its execution is not required to be proved in order to make its certified copy admissible in evidence. He argues that even if the original deed was not produced if it could be proved that the deed was more that 30 years old, then there is no need to prove its execution. 

 14. From the records it appears that one of the executants refused to give her thumb impression but it has not been so stated that she did not sign the document for its execution. The appellate Court found that the said executant must be a genuine executant and so she might have refused to give her thumb impression but that does not mean that she did not execute the document or that she was not the person as claimed by the plaintiff. 

 21. Admittedly he was a Korfa tenant but if the suit is transferred without the consent of the landlord, the landlord may take over the possession under section 48 (f) of the Bengal Tenancy Act but it does not appear that the landlord has so taken over the possession of the suit land. The Korfa tenant or his heirs cannot challenge their own transfer.
